newsitem.title: CHINA: Moody's says may cut some S.Korean debt ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says may cut some S.Korean debt ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday it was reviewing for possible downgrade South Korea's Prime-1 short-term foreign currency ratings and A-1 long-term foreign currency bank deposit ratings.
Moody's also affirmed South Korea's A-1 foreign currency rating for bond obligations.

The Prime-1 rating for short-term deposits and commercial paper and the A1 rating for long-term deposits of Korea Development Bank and Industrial Bank of Korea were also being reviewed for possible downgrade, it said.

The Prime-1 short-term deposit rating and A-1 long-term deposit rating of Housing & Commercial Bank, and Prime-1 commercial paper rating of Export-Import Bank of Korea were being reviewed for possible downgrade.

Moody's said it confirmed the A-1 long-term senior debt rating and E-plus bank financial strength rating of Korea Development Bank and the A-1 long-term senior debt, A-2 subordinated debt and D bank financial strength ratings of Industrial Bank of Korea.
It confirmed the A-1 senior long-term, A-2 subordinated and C-plus bank financial strength ratings of Housing & Commercial Bank, and the long-term senior A-1 rating of Export-Import Bank of Korea.
Moody's said it would review whether South Korea is becoming increasingly vulnerable to a near-term liquidity squeeze as a result of the large and rapid build-up of short-term debt in recent years.

Moody's said its review of South Korea would entail an examination of whether the weakening financial health of the corporate and banking sectors will place additional pressures on the country's external payments position.

The review will also explore the extent to which the on-going deterioration of the economic condition of North Korea adds potential uncertainty to the overall risk profile of South Korea, Moody's said.
It said that the rating outlook for the foreign currency country ceiling for bonds remains negative.
